explanation.summary: Any polynomial satisfying $f(x)f(1/x) = f(x) + f(1/x)$ is of the form $f(x) = 1 \pm x^n$. Given $f(3) = 28 = 1 + 3^3 \implies f(x) = 1 + x^3$. Therefore $f(4) = 1 + 4^3 = 65$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: Any polynomial satisfying $f(x)f(1/x) = f(x) + f(1/x)$ is of the form $f(x) = 1 \pm x^n$. Given $f(3) = 28 = 1 + 3^3 \implies f(x) = 1 + x^3$. Therefore $f(4) = 1 + 4^3 = 65$.
